newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOL, pharma shares push BUX index higher.
newsitem.headline: MOL, pharma shares push BUX index higher.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange closed the week in an upbeat mood as most leading shares saw significant gains and turnover doubled from Thursday.
Oil and gas company MOL Rt accounted for almost one third of 2.63 billion forints' spot share turnover, putting on 80 forints to end at 1,755.

Traders attributed MOL's rally to larger-than-expected energy price rises. The government announced on Thursday an 18.8 percent gas price rise for consumers effective from January 1, while market expectations were around 16 percent.
However, one dealer timism is may be premature.

"It is not yet clear what MOL's share from the price rise will be," said Peter Haas of Postabank Securities. The Hungharian Energy Office said on Friday an announcement on suppliers' margins was unlikely before mid-December.
The two pharmaceuticals shares continued their rise on Friday, with Richter closing a shade higher at 8,475 forints, up 125, closely followed by Egis which gained 110 to end at 8,450.
Chemicals makers Borsodchem and Tiszai Vegyi Kombinat (TVK) moved in opposite directions, Borsodchem gaining 25 forints to close at 3,390 forints while TVK edged lower by 10 forints to 1,380.
"Investors seem to regard the two companies as complementary. When they turn their attention to one, they forget the other," Haas said.
Another dealer said TVK's minor loss on Friday has little significance.
"One cannot draw long-term conclusions from this," said Zsolt Katona of ING Barings.
Haas added that TVK's longer-term prospects are promising.
"It has good signs, a good (Q3) report and good expectations," he said.
